answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Delta Rule. Each identity has a persistent behaviour vector; an agent's delta between epochs must fall inside a bounded grove of historically observed trajectories. Sybil clusters that copy a target's behaviour late show abrupt jumps that flag them, while slow drift past the canyon threshold triggers re-verification. Enforcement: participation rights decay when deltas exceed tolerance across two consecutive epochs. Cost: attackers must sustain consistent costly behaviour per identity for many epochs, multiplying effort linearly per fake agent.
